title: RepoShieldSecurityFixBenchmarkCase
description: Standardized schema for evaluating security fix verification baselines on vulnerable code and candidate patches.

case_id.description: Unique identifier for the benchmark case (e.g. RS-BENCH-001)

origin.description: Dataset source or provenance (e.g. synthetic_curated, cve_adapted, juliet_benchmark)

cve_id.description: Associated Common Vulnerabilities and Exposures identifier if applicable

cwe_id.description: Common Weakness Enumeration identifier (e.g. CWE-89, CWE-78, CWE-22)

vulnerability_category.description: Normalized category of vulnerability (e.g. sql_injection, command_injection, path_traversal, deserialization, broken_access_control, false_positive_finding, tool_failure_timeout)

description.description: Concise summary of the vulnerability and security context

source_file.description: Relative file path of the affected source code module (e.g. src/auth_service.py)

vulnerable_code.description: Complete baseline source code containing the vulnerability or benign target construct

baseline_revision.description: Source revision identifier or SHA-256 hash of the baseline source content

split.description: Evaluation partition separating development tuning examples from held-out evaluation cases

existing_unit_test.description: Existing functional unit test code asserting normal application behavior, or null if unconfigured

targeted_regression_test.description: Targeted security test code asserting non-exploitability of the vulnerability, or null if test evidence is absent

candidate_patches.description: Set of candidate patches representing different real-world fix qualities and adversarial evasions

patch_id.description: Unique identifier for candidate patch (e.g. RS-001-P1)

patch_type.description: Empirical taxonomy of patch quality: true fix, ineffective fix, cosmetic evasion, partial/incomplete fix, functional regression, security regression, false positive finding, missing evidence, or tool failure

ground_truth_label.description: Ground truth: FIX (safe to deploy), NON_FIX (should be blocked), or INCONCLUSIVE (insufficient evidence/tool crash)

ground_truth_rationale.description: Scientific justification explaining why this patch is labeled as FIX, NON_FIX, or INCONCLUSIVE

expected_classification.description: Expected verification verdict: VERIFIED, FAILED, or INCONCLUSIVE

expected_regression_status.description: Expected finding regression classification from comparator

unified_diff.description: Standard unified diff representing the proposed code change

description.description: Explanation of the patch mechanics and why it succeeds or fails
